meta.title: Cookie policy
meta.description: {brand} uses only strictly necessary cookies: no analytics or advertising cookies. See exactly what is stored and why.

title: Cookie policy
intro: {brand} keeps cookies to the minimum needed to run a secure service. Here is everything we store in your browser, and why.

items.i1: We only use cookies that are strictly necessary to sign you in, keep your session secure and take your subscription payment safely.
items.i2: We do not use analytics, advertising or social-media tracking cookies.
items.i3: Booking-page statistics are anonymous and cookieless. Nothing is stored on your customers’ devices.

s2.title: Cookies we use
s2.p1: These cookies are stored under {brand}’s own address (first-party). They are only set for people who sign in to a business account, or are in the middle of doing so.

session.purpose: Keeps you signed in. Holds a random session token only; it cannot be read by page scripts and is only sent over secure connections.
session.duration: Up to 30 days without activity, renewed as you use the app. Removed when you sign out.

business.purpose: Remembers which business you are working in if you belong to more than one.
business.duration: Until you close your browser or sign out.
business.when: After you sign in and switch business

google.purpose: Used only while you sign in with Google. Holds, encrypted, the one-time values that let us recognise Google’s answer as meant for your browser. It cannot be read by page scripts.
google.duration: Ten minutes at most. Removed as soon as the sign-in finishes.

stripe.purpose: Set by Stripe’s payment form, which opens on our billing page when you subscribe. Stripe uses them to prevent payment fraud.
stripe.when: When you open the payment form on the billing page

s2.p2: These cookies are strictly necessary to provide the service you asked for, so under the ePrivacy Directive (art. 5(3)) and Greek law 3471/2006 (art. 4(5)) they do not require consent. That is why we do not show a cookie banner. If we ever add optional cookies, we will ask for your consent first.

s3.title: Local storage
s3.p1: If you choose a colour theme (light, dark or system), we remember that choice in your browser’s local storage under {key}. It stays on your device and is never sent to our servers. You can clear it at any time in your browser settings.

s4.title: Booking pages and the embeddable widget
s4.p1: When customers open a business’s booking page (directly, through a QR code or through the widget embedded on the business’s website), {brand} does not set cookies for analytics or advertising. To show businesses how their booking page performs, we count steps such as “page viewed” and “booking completed” anonymously, without cookies, device identifiers or personal data.
s4.p2: A website that embeds the widget may use its own cookies. Those are controlled by that website, not by {brand}.

s5.title: Payments with Stripe
s5.p1: When a business owner subscribes, Stripe’s payment form opens on our billing page, inside a frame that belongs to Stripe. Managing billing happens on pages hosted by Stripe. In both, Stripe may set its own cookies, for example to prevent fraud, under Stripe’s own cookie and privacy policies.

s6.title: Managing cookies
s6.p1: You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings. If you block the session cookie, you will not be able to sign in to {brand}; booking pages will keep working.

s7.title: Questions
s7.p1: Contact us at <email>{email}</email>. For more on how we handle personal data, see the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.

s8.title: Signing in with Google
s8.p1: If you choose “Continue with Google”, you sign in on a page hosted by Google. Google may set its own cookies there, under Google’s own cookie and privacy policies. We receive no cookies from Google; we only set the short-lived cookie listed above.
